promotionCandidates.title: Resolve the promised shared aggregate-export review against ADR-0005's barrel prohibition

evidence.note: The live module guide says there is no schema or root barrel and explicitly defers a barrel/aggregate export to a separate backlog leaf.
ADR-0005 makes the opposite durable decision: only scoped subpaths are allowed, the schemas barrel stays removed, and the absent root export is actively gated.
The implemented package surface contains wildcard scoped exports and constants, with neither a root dot export nor a schemas aggregate.
A representative consumer needs three defining-file imports across constants, rules, and schemas, illustrating the navigation/API question the deferred review would adjudicate.

promotionCandidates.problem: The live shared guide promises a separate backlog decision about root or schema aggregate exports, while ADR-0005 treats those exports as a prohibited, load-bearing architecture choice. CQ25-115 landed schema-layout work but never performed that promised review. Contributors and audits therefore receive incompatible answers about whether an aggregate entrypoint is intended future work or a forbidden regression.
promotionCandidates.proposedDirection: Perform the bounded design review promised by schemas/MODULE.md. Either define a curated aggregate surface with explicit bundle and dependency-graph safeguards and update ADR-0005 plus its gates, or reaffirm scoped-only imports and remove the deferred-leaf promise.

promotionCandidates.title: dateTimeField-backed mapper boundaries duplicate Date-to-ISO normalization

evidence.note: dateTimeField already accepts either a string or Date and performs the canonical Date.toISOString() normalization.
Both map-layer timestamps use the shared normalizing field.
The detail-path mapper contract is derived as z.input<typeof mapLayerSchema>, allowing Prisma Dates to reach the output parser.
The detail-path map-layer mapper follows the schema-input convention and returns raw Date values.
A second mapper for the same map-layer schema instead hand-normalizes both timestamps, demonstrating two live boundary conventions.
mapCharacterDetail targets the schema output type and repeats ISO conversion even though the inherited character schema uses dateTimeField.

evidence.measurement: `rg -n 'toISOString\(\)' packages/server/src --glob '!*.test.ts' --glob '!*.test.tsx' | wc -l` returns 45; the corresponding `rg -l` command returns 18 files.
evidence.note: This bounds the required inventory; cursor generation, logging, exports, and schemas without dateTimeField are intentionally not all removable.

promotionCandidates.problem: dateTimeField is already the shared Date-to-wire-string boundary, but server mappers alternate between schema-input result types that return Prisma Dates and z.infer output types that force each mapper to call toISOString() itself. The duplicate map-layer paths demonstrate both conventions against one schema. This spreads serialization policy across mapper families and permits equivalent paths to drift.
promotionCandidates.proposedDirection: Inventory entity/DTO mappers whose actual tRPC output schema already uses dateTimeField, derive their result contracts from z.input<typeof schema>, and let output parsing normalize Dates, following MapLayerResult. Preserve cursor/log/export timestamp generation and the prior pack's documented bare-string homebrew/magic-item schemas; split conversions by domain.
